tickets.title: E2 — Decide Cursor permissions and plans with durable delivery guarantees
tickets.body:
## Outcome and scope
A caller or attached human can inspect and answer each real Cursor permission/plan request through existing AD controls, with durable delivery evidence and conservative holds even when child origin is unknown.
Maps PRD AC-6/8/13/15; SR-4.1–4.2, SR-5.1–5.3, SR-9, R2 and closed R3 policy implementation.

## Acceptance criteria / demo
1. Drive actually requested shell, read/write/delete, MCP, web/network, sandbox and child-agent kinds through get-permission/get/list/decide, preserving supplied names, inputs, options and null/absent fields. Fixture coverage is labelled where a kind never requested approval live. Allow selects actual allow-once; deny actual rejection/cancellation, never persistent allow. Unsupported/malformed mappings fail closed visibly.
2. Present real blocking cursor/create_plan content/options using the captured version-specific schema; existing inspection and decide answer it once, check_permission persists while open and a normal turn-end cannot clear it. Demonstrate allow/reject/cancel/timeout and simultaneous plan/permission requests with independent correlation; do not leave ignored extensions hanging indefinitely.
3. Persist the first writer's decision and durably commit each request relay acknowledgement (delivered_at) BEFORE emitting ANY relay ACP answer, including a denial. Instrument/fault-inject the boundary: failed/missing acknowledgement means zero relay ACP response; crash after acknowledgement may show delivered without Cursor receipt. A stored decision or pipe write alone is not acknowledgement. Delivered never claims receipt, acceptance, tool execution or dialog closure, and no second ACP acceptance acknowledgement is required.
4. Demonstrate finite confirm_by and truthful delivered/not_confirmed/fallen_back for store failure, timeout, delayed acknowledgement, disconnect, crash before/after response and AD caller restart. Per-request relay lifecycle/evidence is independent of the long-lived gateway; never use its live pid as a live request hook. No evidence cannot extend uncertainty forever; absent acknowledgement settles to truthful fallen_back. Never retry an uncertain allow as undelivered.
5. Race identical/conflicting API decisions, pane answers, cancellation and timeout across two simultaneous requests and stale launch/conversation ids. Exactly the intended request receives at most one answer; timeout denies/cancels before late approval can execute. Store/transport failures are never approval.
6. With relay on and off, demonstrate connected pane fallback using actual choices and record-pane-answer's existing claim/proof distinction and stale-pane/hash guards. A disconnected pane reports failure rather than claiming delivery. Plain send-keys and pause stay guarded; retain documented capture-to-delivery/request-write race limitations.
7. Persist main-turn-end proof eligibility independently from child id. An authenticated launch-owned request with unknown origin and null agent_id remains child-safe before and after restart/migration. Main turn end and child turn/session/completion/interruption never release child/unknown holds; only valid correlated tool-execution proof or owning-spawn end can. Proven-main age/identity guards still work; subagent requests do not replace main conversation and listing remains untracked.
8. Direct cursor/ask_question, multi-question/multi-select and session/request_permission question fallback are automatically denied before relay/pane approvals; never advertise support. Test fresh/load, both setting values, enabling policies, relay off, attempted caller allow, persistent choices, malformed/ambiguous schema and concurrent genuine permissions. Use supported rejection/cancellation, not method-not-found alone; genuine permission/plan holds survive question denial. Clearly label synthetic/source-derived question fixtures; R3 is closed by product decision, never reopen pre-execution prevention or claim unobserved live denial.

## Implementation/test and doc owners
Reuse permission.go, relayJudge/spawnRequests, decide, record-pane-answer and request_proof paths. Extend SeedDecideFixtureAgent, SeedRelayRequest/newPAEnvAgent and cursorfix, including durable origin proof options rather than cloned suites. If new proof metadata requires a schema hop, migrate historical semantics safely and test all readers/writers plus restart recovery. Extend decide_delivery/sendkeys_hold/record_pane_answer behavioral tests and existing formal relay invariants where affected; any model-check evidence is scheduled externally. Own integration slug cursor-relay. docs/permissions.md owns delivery/holds/question denial; docs/settings.md owns setting effect; docs/caller-contract.md/operator-actions.md own failure/recovery; docs/usage.md owns normal relay use; architecture owns durable acknowledgement and proof eligibility.

This is a draft capability Epic, not authorization to build now. Future implementation must leave the codebase working and all existing tests passing; preserve Claude/Codex behavior and the final t1.ssz.qi amendments. Use existing composition/classifier/store/API seams, machine-readable errors, conditional launch/life writes, parameterized SQL, protected paths and no secret or raw-label leakage. ## Context
Shared cursorfix and actual adapter admission. This group exclusively owns question-specific fallback and ambiguous schemas.

## What Needs to Change
Parameterize direct/multi/multiselect/fallback questions under both settings, relay modes, enabling policies and persistent choices, including allow attempts and concurrent genuine requests. Pin initialization and fresh/load policy fixtures, with actual load reserved for E4.

## Key Files
- cursorhostprotocol/questionpolicy/sessiontests; cursorfix runtime/factory/provenance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Questions are denied before answerable admission/pane/relay through supported rejection/cancellation, never method-not-found alone. No setting/caller/persistent choice can approve them. Genuine holds remain, no ask_user/fabricated answer and no E2 live-load claim.

Relay settlement retires the relay controller and all its queued responses, including allow and deny; it does not resolve a genuinely open connected native request. A deliberate fallen-back pane answer may use the same request arbiter, but terminal timeout/cancellation cannot revive a request and uncertain relay approval is never replayed as a pane answer. Failed/missing acknowledgement means zero relay ACP replies, including timeout denial: use separately validated cancellation or truthful bounded failure/fallback, never disguise a denial as cancellation. Preserve conservative holds until valid proof or owning-spawn end.

tickets.title: PRD
tickets.body:
# Cursor support in agent-director

## Problem Statement

Users with a Cursor budget cannot manage Cursor agents through agent-director (AD) with the state tracking, permission relay, lifecycle controls and groups available to Claude Code and Codex users. They need the same AD workflow for Cursor.

## Goals

- Add Cursor with feature parity with AD's Claude Code and Codex support, including state tracking, permission relay, kill, pause, resume and groups.
- Run Cursor inside the agent tmux pane, the common substrate for AD agents, whichever route the SRD chooses.
- Keep the product as simple as parity permits, extending existing AD controls and caller contracts.

## Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- A replacement transcript display.
- Repeating b.ssz's generic naming migration or implementing Codex again.
- New billing controls, model purchasing or account administration.
- Features beyond existing AD parity unless stated here.

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**Existing AD contract and agent selection.**

- This work builds on b.ssz and PRD t1.ssz.qi, including its final approved amendments of 2026-10-12. Their generic agent selection, naming, launch-path, template, environment, pre-trust, ownership and lifecycle rules apply to Cursor. Those final amendments take precedence over older dependency text.
- Callers can explicitly select `cursor` wherever an agent is selected, including templates. Cursor appears as the row's agent on the existing CLI, MCP, library, client and operator surfaces. There is no default agent.
- Cursor uses the same argument and template precedence rules as the existing agents. Arguments must not silently override AD's required behavior or change the SRD-selected launch route into another operating mode.
- Users can install and use AD on a host with Cursor as its only supported agent. Cursor has the same optional launch-path control and missing-program behavior as the existing agents.

**Interaction and state.**

- Cursor runs inside its agent tmux pane; users can inspect the pane with `read-pane`.
- Users must be able to attach to the agent tmux pane and take over by typing into Cursor normally, whichever route the SRD chooses.
- `send-keys` submits a multiline message intact as one prompt. Repeated sends do not duplicate earlier text or join it to the next message. Existing safeguards for pending agents and possible dialogs still apply.
- Cursor rows use AD's existing states with their existing meanings. Callers can distinguish work in progress, readiness for input, a permission decision, an ended agent and a missing agent. Question behavior follows the contract below.
- A fresh Cursor session reports in when its session starts. A login screen stays `pending`; a running agent that has not reported stays `pending`, noted `unreported`. Resume does not require an immediate startup report and may stay pending until the next prompt.
- A completed or interrupted turn returns the row to the appropriate existing state. Only the row's own agent may change its state; unrelated agents and their activity must not change it.
- Session identity, transcript access and history follow the active conversation. Cursor's `/clear` and `/new` preserve prior-session history within the current life and move the row to the new conversation when reported. Activity by a subagent does not replace the main conversation.

**Permissions and questions.**

- Cursor supports AD's permission relay, including `check_permission`, inspecting a request, allowing or denying it, delivery status, fallback to the pane and recording a pane answer. This covers every kind of permission request in the supported Cursor experience, including requests arising from subagents.
- Callers receive the requested action and available inputs without fabricated details. Decisions apply only to the intended open request and follow AD's existing duplicate-decision and delivery guarantees.
- Permission handling retains AD's existing fail-closed guarantees, timeout behavior and protection against sending ordinary prompts or pausing through unresolved dialogs. A failure or uncertain delivery must not be reported as a successful approval.
- Caller and template permission lists are either honored or clearly refused with actionable guidance to Cursor's own permission rules. No entry is silently ignored; unsupported lists are refused both when creating a template and when launching from a call or template.
- Gabe’s superseding decision, 2026-10-13, R3 option (a): accept question tool off in practice. The cursor-host gateway never advertises question support; any question that reaches AD, including one that falls back to a permission request, is denied automatically; docs describe Cursor as question tool off, enforced by denial, rather than never offered. This applies with `disable_ask_user` on or off, fresh or resumed, and under enabling policies. Questions are never offered for caller/pane approval. This accepted Cursor-specific amendment replaces the earlier pre-execution prevention/native-availability promise; Claude/Codex behavior is unchanged.

**Lifecycle and history.**

- `pause` ends Cursor's current session under the existing pause contract. `kill` retains AD's strict ownership checks and exact success guarantees: it affects only the intended launch and does not claim success when the existing contract requires failure.
- Existing documented limits of kill remain explicit, including work started by an agent that can survive a successful kill. A surviving hook must not be mistaken for a living main agent or be allowed to change a later launch's state.
- `resume` continues only the last agent's latest reported conversation with its saved configuration. A missing latest conversation is reported without falling back to an older one.
- Same-agent reuse preserves session history and subagent records within the current life. Switching to or from Cursor starts a new life and permanently gives up AD resume of earlier sessions; switching back never restores them. A switching launch that asks to resume starts fresh without error, with dropped arguments reported under the inherited contract.
- Session history and subagent records show only the current life. AD-agent children remain associated with their parent across a switch. Failed reuse, permission-request cleanup and the trail retain the dependency's final amended behavior.
- Cursor supports the existing lifecycle, status, cleanup, labels, help, trail and administration operations on all corresponding AD surfaces. The subagent view either shows accurate supported Cursor subagent information or explicitly reports tracking unsupported with no subagents, under the existing contract. It must not invent activity, states or an unknown state. Subagent permission relay remains required independently of tracking support. Codex remains untracked with no subagents shown.
- With help enabled, Cursor receives the existing AD guidance at session start and after session changes. Guidance is restored after compaction, or documentation records the difference as permitted by the inherited contract. A Cursor caller can use AD's CLI and MCP workflows with correct parent-child association and the same tmux-server behavior as other AD callers.

**Groups and accounts.**

- Many Cursor agents can run concurrently using one group's login and rules. Another group can use a different login and rules without acquiring the first group's credentials or group-specific settings.
- Authentication renewal for one agent must not invalidate another agent's login or overwrite the user's personal login. AD lifecycle operations do not sign users out or alter personal account configuration.
- Group setup and reuse fit the existing environment and template workflow. Resume retains the original group's configuration and conversation.
- Users receive a clear explanation of which personal, project or organization policies also apply and their precedence. Group configuration must not be described as a stronger isolation boundary than the product provides.
- Users can run the models available to their Cursor account against their Cursor budget. Documentation explains the account and billing context, including when a separately configured provider bills elsewhere, without adding AD billing controls.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- Missing programs, login requirements, invalid configuration, invalid arguments and failed launches produce the existing corresponding AD outcomes and actionable errors; nothing silently substitutes another agent or account.
- A stale session identity on exit after `/clear` or `/new` must not leave an exited agent classified as live, or a continuing agent classified as ended. Session changes and resume retain the ownership guarantees.
- Interrupted turns, human answers at the pane, relay delivery failures and timeouts preserve the existing caller safeguards and expose the outcome accurately.
- Authentication expiry or group configuration problems must not silently fall back to another group's or the user's personal credentials.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- Liveness is determined from processes, and no screen text is classified to infer states, dialogs or prompts.
- Cursor support preserves AD's existing ownership, security, privacy and secret-handling guarantees. Existing Claude Code and Codex behavior remains compatible with the final approved dependency contract.
- Spawn, resume and other operations remain within existing client time limits on AD-supported hosts where Cursor runs.

### UI/UX Requirements

- Existing help and documentation explain selecting Cursor, installation, launch configuration, groups, permissions, recovery and the latest-session resume rule alongside the corresponding existing-agent guidance.
- Status and errors use AD's existing vocabulary and distinguish pending startup from readiness. Cursor runs inside the agent tmux pane regardless of the selected route.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cursor can be selected directly or through a template on all existing caller surfaces; precedence, validation and no-default behavior match the inherited contract, and rows identify Cursor correctly.
- [ ] A Cursor-only installation works, the launch-path setting is honored, and missing or invalid launches produce the expected AD outcomes.
- [ ] Cursor runs inside the agent tmux pane; `read-pane` and successive multiline `send-keys` work without lost, duplicated or glued text.
- [ ] Users can attach to the agent tmux pane and take over by typing into Cursor normally, whichever route the SRD chooses, with documentation explaining human takeover.
- [ ] Fresh launch reports at session startup; login and unreported startup remain pending; resumed sessions can remain pending until prompted; working, waiting, permission and terminal states retain their documented meanings.
- [ ] Every supported Cursor permission kind can be inspected and answered through AD. Allow, deny, timeout, duplicate decision, uncertain delivery, pane fallback and recorded human answers preserve existing relay and prompt-safety guarantees.
- [ ] Caller and template permission-list entries are honored or refused with actionable guidance to Cursor's own rules; unsupported entries are refused at template creation and at launch, including from a saved template, and none are silently ignored.
- [ ] The Cursor gateway never advertises question support and automatically denies every question reaching AD, including permission fallback, for both suppression setting values, fresh/resumed sessions and enabling policies. Caller or pane approvals cannot answer a question. Documentation says question tool off, enforced by denial, and does not claim never offered (Gabe’s 2026-10-13 R3 option (a)).
- [ ] Pause ends the intended session; kill meets its existing ownership and success contract, including errors and documented survivor limits; unrelated launches are untouched and surviving hooks cannot change a later launch's state.
- [ ] `/clear` and `/new` rotate conversation identity and history correctly; stale exit identities never leave a dead agent live or a continuing agent ended.
- [ ] Resume restores the latest conversation and group configuration only; a missing latest conversation is reported without fallback. Same-agent reuse retains history, switches clear the current life's history, and switching back with a resume request starts fresh without reviving earlier sessions. AD-agent children remain listed across switches.
- [ ] Concurrent agents in one group share its login and rules while another group uses its own; renewal and lifecycle operations preserve other agents' and the user's personal login, and failures never silently use another account.
- [ ] The Cursor subagent view shows accurate supported information or explicitly reports tracking unsupported with no subagents; it invents no activity or states, including an unknown state. Subagent permissions are relayed regardless of tracking support, and Codex remains untracked with no subagents shown.
- [ ] Existing lifecycle and administration surfaces, labels, trail and Cursor-originated CLI/MCP child launches satisfy the existing AD contracts. With help enabled, guidance appears at session start and after session changes; after compaction it is restored or the difference is documented.
- [ ] Documentation covers the Cursor workflow, recovery, group-policy precedence and billing context; no group isolation or operation outcome is overstated. Claude and Codex contracts remain intact, and operations meet existing time limits without screen-based state classification.

## Assumptions

- b.ssz and the final approved amendments to t1.ssz.qi provide the baseline; this PRD adds Cursor to that product contract.
- Risk for the SRD: the SRD chooses the terminal or ACP route after a research round, and must meet the parity requirements.

tickets.title: SRD
tickets.body:
# Cursor support: software requirements

Basis: approved PRD `t1.ftd.y5`, the final approved 2026-10-12 amendments to `t1.ssz.qi`, and agent-director 0.12.0 at `ccb41e075695609b084292f52c36512f3665d210`. The final amendments override earlier dependency wording. The PRD's acceptance criteria are numbered AC-1 through AC-15 in their listed order below.

Gabe's design decision, 2026-10-13: **AD ships a small gateway CLI, working name `agent-director cursor-host`, as the Cursor row's own tmux pane process.** It hosts Cursor over ACP and provides the interactive terminal. This names the design; it does not claim implementation or acceptance evidence. The [ACP host recommendation](../../research/cursor-state-tracking/report-2-acp.md), sections 1 and 4–5, supplies the durable pipe-owning host design. Its output-only renderer is extended here to satisfy ordinary attach-and-type takeover. [Research findings](cursor-route-findings-2026-10-13.md) and [authenticated live checks](live-checks-2026-10-13.md) are the evidence records. Linux Cursor `2026.10.12-d47ca18` negotiated ACP 1 and established real interactivity, permissions, persistence and an isolated MCP caller path through an out-of-repository prototype. SR-11.2 closes those measured subchecks and retains the unmet parts of each full gate. **R3 is closed by Gabe’s 2026-10-13 option (a) decision: question tool off in practice, enforced by automatic denial. R1/R2/R4/R6 have sufficient route feasibility evidence for planning; their production build and acceptance work is not complete. R5 retains explicitly NOT CHECKED LIVE credential/platform limitations and conditional operator acceptance.** The later R3 decision overrides the earlier prevention/native-availability requirement for Cursor only; all other parity requirements remain required.

## SR-0: Cursor gateway CLI design

### SR-0.1: Launch and protocol ownership
- AD installs/ships `agent-director cursor-host` with its CLI and launches it directly as the row's recorded tmux pane process on the existing selected server. The gateway is the tracked main process for this Cursor route, not an external AD caller or an arbitrary user wrapper.
- One gateway starts one `cursor-agent acp` runtime (the executable selected by `cursor_path`, default `agent` on PATH) with the row's saved cwd, validated arguments and group environment. It owns the child's stdin/stdout for the entire launch; ACP JSON-RPC pipes are never the human terminal input/output.
- The gateway performs `initialize`, fresh `session/new` or latest-only `session/load`, sends queued `session/prompt` calls, consumes `session/update` and handles cancellation. It answers `session/request_permission`, `cursor/ask_question` and blocking `cursor/create_plan` calls on AD's behalf under SR-5, including actual pane answers and fail-closed unsupported requests.
- The gateway feeds authoritative state, session ids, transcript references and permission requests through AD's existing store/hook paths, conditional launch/life writes and trails. State comes from correlated protocol requests/replies and process evidence. Cursor's absent ACP lifecycle hooks are not a dependency. Optional Cursor tool hooks do not acquire the right to report lifecycle from a child process.
- The gateway emits required hook reports with the gateway itself as their immediate parent, so the recorded pane pid/start-time gate remains intact. It must authenticate its owned ACP runtime/connection and owning launch before reporting protocol activity. Main/child origin is reported only when independently proven; launch-owned requests with unknown origin may be relayed under the conservative SR-5.2 proof rules, without invented child ids. No grandparent matching, arbitrary wrapper adoption or bypass of the existing gate is permitted.
- Restarting an AD CLI/MCP caller leaves the gateway, its owned pipes, active conversation and pending decisions intact. Any host-local transport needed for reconnection is private to the current launch, checks its identity and cannot bypass existing AD request/decision safeguards; it is not a new public control API.

### SR-0.2: Interactive terminal and transcript
- The gateway renders current Cursor text, tool activity and decisions in its own pane, and accepts normal typing, multiline paste, permission/plan answers and interruption. A person can attach and use this pane as with Claude or Codex. Both human input and existing `send-keys` reach this one input controller; ordinary follow-ups are queued rather than cancelling an active ACP turn.
- The gateway implements `/clear`, `/new` and `/exit` as local terminal commands with SR-3.3/SR-6 confirmation and history rules; it does not forward them blindly as model prompts. Protocol request identity binds displayed choices to their answers.
- The gateway writes the transcript Cursor does not write in ACP mode: ordered user input, Cursor updates, decisions and outcomes, with launch/conversation attribution and protected access. SR-6 governs history, truthful availability and replay deduplication; SR-7 forbids credential leakage. Persistence/transport failure must be visible and cannot invent saved history or accepted decisions.
- AD never reads or interprets screen text to derive state, permissions, questions, session identity or liveness. `read-pane` remains explicit human/caller inspection; its existing capture/hash guards protect input without classifying the displayed text.

### SR-0.3: Pane identity and coupled lifetime
- Because the gateway is the row's pane process, `kill`, `find-missing`, `read-pane`, `send-keys` and pane identity checks retain their existing process/label/server contracts and strict gate. These verbs do not adopt the ACP child as an unrelated pane owner.
- The gateway must detect its Cursor child's exit by pid/start time and owned-process exit evidence, stop accepting prompts/approvals and terminate itself with truthful end reporting. A live renderer cannot keep a dead Cursor launch live. Pipe EOF alone is a transport failure, not proof of process death.
- Gateway shutdown cancels unresolved calls and ends only its owned runtime/processes under existing kill guarantees. A gateway crash must not leave an untracked Cursor conversation accepting work; parent-loss cleanup and any surviving worker limits require R1 evidence. The live pending-permission crash left an unguarded ACP child alive; the Linux parent-death guard stopped it. A platform-appropriate guard must be in effect before the owned child can accept work and must cover the executable/launcher chain. A transport close cannot substitute for this guard. The Linux prototype is not macOS evidence. No process-group operation may kill another row's shared worker or group member.

## SR-1: Agent selection and public contracts

### SR-1.1: Selection and row representation
- `cursor` is a valid, case-sensitive agent value everywhere `claude` and `codex` are accepted: `internal/config`, `internal/spawn`, `internal/store`, `pkg/api`, CLI/admin, MCP schemas/dispatch, templates, and the TypeScript client.
- A per-call agent overrides the template's agent; a template can supply an omitted agent. No config, environment setting or implicit fallback supplies a default agent.
- Missing or unknown selection retains `ErrAgentMissing` or `ErrAgentInvalid`; validation failures launch nothing and write no row or template.
- `get`, `list`, status-related row output, persisted rows, trails and client/library representations identify Cursor using the existing generic agent fields. Existing rows retain their agent and data.
- Existing verb names, generic field names, errors, labels, result envelopes and admin operations remain available with their existing meanings; this work introduces no alternate Cursor-only control plane.

### SR-1.2: Arguments and templates
- Existing precedence and presence semantics in `internal/spawn` and `internal/config/template_file.go` apply: per-call arguments replace template arguments; MCP/Go explicitly empty lists replace them, while CLI/TypeScript empty lists retain their existing absent-input meaning.
- A template with arguments must name their agent. Inheriting arguments for another agent fails with the existing argument-agent mismatch error.
- Cursor argument validation covers accepted aliases and combined/value forms and rejects changes to AD-required operating mode, ownership, session selection, question suppression or mandatory integration behavior with the existing refused-argument error naming the offending argument.
- Ordinary supported Cursor model and permission controls remain pass-through inputs where they preserve AD's required behavior; AD must not silently translate an explicit argument into a different policy or operating mode.
- Cursor session-picking/resume arguments are refused on plain spawn and same-agent reuse. A switching reuse drops all such arguments, reports them in `dropped_args`, and starts fresh without error. Resume does not replay them.
- A supported initial prompt in arguments reaches Cursor once and follows existing saved-argument replay behavior on resume; it must not be mistaken for a subcommand or silently discarded by ACP. R6 showed positional prompt text before `acp` exits before initialization: the gateway extracts supported prompt text and submits it through `session/prompt`, rather than forwarding it as Cursor argv. Any accepted explicit mode must be authoritatively selected through the supported route or refused clearly: `--plan` and `--mode plan` alone started ACP sessions in agent mode on the tested build. Model selection was honored; acceptance of a flag alone does not establish its effect.
- Make-template and launch both refuse any Cursor `allow`, `deny` or `ask` list entry with `ErrPermissionsUnsupported` and actionable guidance to Cursor's own permission rules. This includes hand-edited/saved templates and merged call/template lists; empty lists and `disable_ask_user` alone are not refused.

## SR-2: Installation and launch configuration

### SR-2.1: Programs and supported versions
- `install.sh` succeeds with Cursor as the only installed supported agent; Claude/Codex-only setup is skipped accurately and no other agent is required to launch Cursor.
- `internal/config/config.go` exposes an optional `[launch] cursor_path`, with the same type, validation, effective-at-launch behavior and whole-path treatment as the existing agent paths. Unset, the Cursor program is `agent` on PATH.

## SR-3: Real pane interaction

### SR-3.1: Human takeover
- Every Cursor row owns a real tmux pane on the existing AD-selected server. Attaching to it exposes readable current Cursor output and an editable prompt accepting ordinary typing without another AD command or external application.

- This work adds no replacement transcript browsing product; transcript access and pane inspection remain the existing AD surfaces.

### SR-3.2: Automated and human input
- `send-keys` submits successive multiline messages as distinct complete prompts, preserving newlines and Unicode without dropped, duplicated or carried-over text. Bracketed paste and Enter behavior must be tested with the actual interactive pane.
- Human and automated submissions have one observable order. A subsequent ordinary prompt must not cancel the current turn merely because Cursor ACP replaces an in-flight prompt; follow-up input retains the existing supported queuing behavior.
- Every queued submission is bound to its launch and confirmed conversation at acceptance. Ordinary submissions run FIFO after the current turn and outstanding decisions finish; a queued submission never migrates to a new conversation. Terminal control commands and interruption take priority over waiting ordinary submissions, while retaining observable input order.
- Interruption cancels the current turn, its outstanding decisions and all not-yet-started submissions; the gateway visibly identifies each cancelled queued submission and does not restart work automatically. `/clear` and `/new` first cancel that work and queue, then request a new session; input during rotation is held from submission until the new identity is confirmed, and a failed rotation visibly refuses that input rather than sending it to either conversation. `/exit` and pause cancel queued submissions visibly before shutdown. Kill/crash recovery never automatically replays unstarted transient pane/send-keys submissions as new work. Saved initial-prompt arguments retain the existing resume replay contract in SR-1.2; that explicit exception does not restore the transient input queue.
- Existing `allow_pending`, pane hash, dialog-maybe-open and permission-answer safeguards in `pkg/api/sendkeys.go`, `pkg/api/pause.go` and pane-answer operations apply unchanged, with their documented limits in `docs/permissions.md`: a dialog can appear between capture and key delivery or before its first request write. Cursor must preserve these safeguards and disclose these limits; this requirement does not promise to eliminate those races.
- A pane fallback offers actual choices for the intended request while the connection can still accept its answer. If that connection is gone, the pane reports the failure; AD never claims an answer reached Cursor.

### SR-3.3: Terminal commands
- `/clear` and `/new` typed in the pane start a new Cursor conversation within the current life, preserve prior history and update the row only upon authoritative confirmation of the new identity.
- `/exit` typed in the pane ends the intended Cursor session; it is not sent to the model as prompt text. It leaves the row terminal only when the session has actually ended.
- Interruption cancels the intended current work and its outstanding decisions, preserves conversation identity, and returns to the appropriate existing state after confirmation.

## SR-4: State, ownership and process liveness

### SR-4.1: State meanings
- Cursor uses the existing states only. A new launch is `pending` until its own authenticated conversation startup is confirmed; a login screen or running launch with no report remains `pending`, noted `unreported` under the existing timing rules.
- Fresh startup reports without requiring a user prompt. Resume may remain pending until the next prompt; it may not fabricate a startup event to satisfy a timer.
- Confirmed input processing yields `working`, completed or interrupted turns yield `waiting` when no unresolved higher-priority dialog remains, and permission requests yield `check_permission`.
- A blocking plan approval yields `check_permission` and uses the existing permission-request inspection/decision surfaces under SR-5.1. Clearing one request never clears another; Cursor question attempts are automatically denied under SR-5.3 and do not open an answerable `ask_user` dialog. Ordinary turn completion does not clear a still-open plan decision.
- Cursor does not enter `ask_user` to await a question answer: every question attempt is automatically denied, even with `disable_ask_user` off. Concurrent genuine permission/plan requests retain their own state and holds; denying a question never resolves them.
- An intentional completed session yields `ended`; an unexpectedly absent main agent follows existing `missing`/find-missing rules. A transport error alone does not prove process death or successful termination.

### SR-4.2: Authoritative identity
- Only activity attributable to the current row's launch may mutate it. The identity contract includes the store, instance id, launch token, life, tmux server/pane and relevant process start times.
- `internal/tmux`, `internal/probe`, `internal/store` conditional writes and the protections represented by `internal/hook/gate.go` retain their existing strength for every agent. Cursor event handling must reject stale, unrelated, nested hand-started and previous-launch reports.
- Liveness is determined from process evidence, never screen content. The tracked gateway must terminate when its owned Cursor child exits, as required by SR-0.3; a surviving renderer, worker or hook cannot keep that launch live.
- Missing/unreadable identity or conflicting ownership retains existing conservative error/unknown-evidence behavior; it does not authorize adoption or killing another launch.
- A stale conversation id on exit after `/clear` or `/new` cannot leave a dead launch live, and an old-conversation completion cannot end a continuing launch. Process and conversation identity are distinct facts.
- A child-agent session id never replaces the main conversation id, transcript or history. **R1/R2 remaining:** a live child-shell permission arrived on the owned connection with the main sessionId; a later task notification named the child. This does not establish arbitrary child/nested-child provenance or tool-execution proof. Authenticated owning-launch/ACP-connection attribution remains required even when subagent listing is disabled. Main/child origin may remain unknown; relaying that launch-owned request is allowed, with durable child-safe proof eligibility under SR-5.2 and no invented child identity.

Gabe’s superseding R3 decision, 2026-10-13, option (a): **accept question tool off in practice. The cursor-host gateway never advertises question support; any question that reaches AD, including one that falls back to a permission request, is denied automatically; docs describe Cursor as question tool off, enforced by denial, rather than never offered.** This explicitly supersedes the earlier pre-execution-prevention decision and Cursor’s PRD AC-8 native-availability promise. Claude/Codex question behavior is unchanged.

## SR-5: Permissions, delivery and questions

### SR-5.1: Complete request coverage
- Every permission request raised by the supported Cursor route is represented through existing permission inspection/decision surfaces, including shell, file read/write/delete, MCP, web/network, sandbox and child-agent requests where Cursor asks for approval.
- Tool names, supplied input, action descriptions and available choices reflect the actual request. Missing fields remain absent/null according to existing schemas; AD does not invent commands, paths, tool ids or approval choices.
- AD allow means the request's allow-once choice, and deny means its rejection/cancellation choice. AD does not silently choose allow-always or write a persistent Cursor rule. Native persistent choices offered explicitly at the pane retain their documented group-wide effect.
- A blocking `cursor/create_plan` approval is represented as an open request in the existing `get-permission`, `get`/`list` permission fields and `decide` surfaces, with `check_permission` state, prompt/pause safeguards, request identity, deadlines and delivery/fallback rules from SR-5.2. AD allow means accepting this plan once; deny means rejecting/cancelling this plan, never granting a persistent policy. The pane presents its actual plan and choices. R2 captured real blocking plan requests with toolCallId/name/overview/plan/todos/isProject/phases and accepted/rejected response objects, after which turns completed. Use the captured version-specific schema, preserving absent fields and correlating by the protocol request. Cancellation semantics and the production AD permission/delivery mapping still require validation; absent a validated mapping, fail closed visibly rather than fabricate options, silently approve, treat it as output or leave an ignored extension awaiting forever.
- Unknown or malformed authorization requests fail closed, expose an actionable error and preserve the pending decision where possible. Unsupported notification data cannot authorize a tool.

### SR-5.2: Existing relay guarantees
- `get-permission`, `decide`, `record-pane-answer` and permission data in `get`/`list` retain the contracts implemented by `internal/store/permission.go`, `pkg/api/relay_delivery.go`, `pkg/api/decide.go` and pane-answer operations.
- Decisions are bound to one open request in one launch/conversation; duplicate identical and conflicting decisions have the existing outcomes. Concurrent requests, cancellation, timeout and pane/API races cannot deliver an answer to a different request or deliver two answers.
- Delivery retains `delivered`, `not_confirmed` and `fallen_back` with their existing meanings, finite `confirm_by` bound and truthful evidence fields. The gateway request relay durably commits its per-request acknowledgement (`delivered_at`) before handing any relay answer to Cursor over ACP. No successful acknowledgement means no relay ACP answer may be emitted. `delivered` means that relay acknowledgement, not proof of Cursor receipt, runtime acceptance, tool execution or dialog closure; a crash after acknowledgement can leave delivered without Cursor receipt, as under the inherited contract. A recorded decision or pipe write alone is not acknowledgement. Without acknowledgement, finite request-relay termination/settlement yields truthful `fallen_back`; connected pane fallback remains available under the existing guards.
- A long-lived ACP/terminal process must not be reported as a live per-request relay hook. Existing nullable process-evidence fields must represent actual evidence, and missing evidence must not prolong uncertainty indefinitely or imply successful delivery.
- Relay timeout denies/cancels before a timed-out relay could allow execution. Store failures, disconnects and crashes do not become approval; uncertain delivery is never retried as though known not delivered.
- Falling back leaves a real request answerable at the pane when Cursor is still connected. Pane answers and externally recorded human answers retain their existing claim/proof distinction and stale-pane protections.
- Plain `send-keys` and `pause` retain the dialog holds and proof rules in `internal/store/request_proof.go` and `docs/permissions.md`. A main-agent turn-end proof applies only to eligible main-agent requests under the existing request-age and identity guards; it never releases a child's hold.
- A child request’s hold ends only with valid correlated tool-execution proof or the end of its owning AD spawn. Child turn, session, completion, interruption or other lifecycle events alone never release it. Launch-owned requests whose main/child origin is unknown are relayable but retain the same child-safe holds without fabricated child ids. Persist proof eligibility separately from absent child identity: an unknown origin must never become eligible for main-turn-end proof merely because `agent_id` is null. The exact representation is an implementation choice; all proof writers/readers and restart recovery must preserve this distinction. Proven main origin, tool-call correlation and launch identity are required before the corresponding proof applies.
- With relay off, Cursor's actual permission choices remain usable at the pane and pending dialogs remain protected from ordinary prompt/pause actions.
- **R2 route feasibility supported / production acceptance outstanding:** authenticated requests covered shell, delete, web search, MCP, child-shell and plan approval, including one-shot allow/reject, an 80-second hold, cancellation and a connected typed answer. Workspace read/write and direct web fetch ran without requesting approval in the tested configuration; no approval schema is invented for them. Client stdin EOF left a blocked process alive. These observations do not establish AD per-request relay evidence, finite deadlines, durable delivery/ack semantics, race behavior, after-acceptance loss or all requested approval kinds. Those guarantees remain mandatory before parity is claimed.

### SR-5.3: Question-tool policy
- The cursor-host gateway never advertises question support in ACP initialization, for fresh or loaded sessions. This is not a claim that Cursor cannot offer or invoke the tool.
- Every question reaching AD is denied automatically, including `cursor/ask_question`, multi-question/multi-select requests and question requests routed through `session/request_permission`. This applies with `disable_ask_user` on or off, under enabling project/group policy and on resume. The setting remains accepted under the generic contract but cannot enable Cursor questions.

Never return method-not-found as the sole defense: extension failure may trigger permission fallback, which must also be denied. Unrecognized or ambiguous question/authorization schemas fail closed visibly; they cannot be presented as ordinary answerable permissions until validated as non-question requests.
- Question denial precedes relay/pane handling, so no caller allow, persistent rule, human pane answer or relay-off fallback can approve a question. Preserve request correlation, finite deadlines, honest delivery and independent genuine permission/plan holds. Do not fabricate a successful answer or record denial delivery without evidence.
- Documentation describes **Cursor question tool off, enforced by denial**, not “never offered.” Show an actionable denied outcome when an attempt arrives; no new question API or answerable question state is added.
- **R3 CLOSED BY PRODUCT DECISION, not live prevention proof.** The prior positive-control attempts emitted no question and source inspection showed extension-to-permission fallback. That evidence is retained. ## SR-6: Lifecycle, history and recovery

### SR-6.1: Pause, kill and restart
- `pause` ends the intended session and preserves its latest resumable conversation, subject to the existing pending/dialog guards. It cannot return success while Cursor continues the session.
- `kill` retains strict ownership checks, exact success/failure guarantees, lookup/disagreement behavior and errors in `pkg/api/kill.go`; it affects no other launch, shared group member or unrelated worker.
- Successful kill has the existing documented limits for independently surviving work. Such survivors cannot mutate the ended launch or a replacement launch, and are not treated as the main agent.
- `find-missing`, `expire`, labels, cleanup and admin actions retain their existing process-only contracts. Termination closes obsolete permission requests using the existing denial and proof rules.
- Loss/restart of an AD command or MCP server does not destroy a live Cursor session. Loss of its interactive runtime is detected honestly, with resume/recovery available only for the latest durably saved conversation.

### SR-6.2: Latest-session resume and current life
- `resume` accepts only the row id and restores its saved Cursor agent, arguments, environment, cwd/group and latest reported conversation. A missing latest conversation or transcript is reported without falling back to older history or silently starting fresh.
- ACP history replay cannot create duplicate user messages, duplicate permission decisions, spurious state transitions or repeated old-session history entries.
- Session/transcript identifiers refer to the real active conversation. Transcript availability is truthful and remains usable through existing history fields even though the researched ACP version did not write a native transcript.
- Same-agent reuse, resume, `/clear` and `/new` retain the life and its history; same-agent reuse retains subagent records under the generic contract.
- Switching to or from Cursor starts a new life with empty prior-session history and subagent records. Switching back never restores AD access to earlier sessions; a switching resume argument starts fresh and is reported as dropped.
- AD-agent children remain associated through `parent_id` across every switch. Permission requests are cleaned on reuse, and append-only trail entries retain all lives.
- A failed reuse that is successfully undone restores the prior agent, life and history; an indeterminate launch retains the existing non-restoration outcome. Cursor extends existing restoration tests rather than changing the rule.
- **R4 subchecks closed:** isolated native store.db creation, graceful and SIGKILL/restart load, marker recall and a nonexistent-session error (-32602) were observed. The gateway owns its separate transcript because native store.db is not a JSONL transcript. Load replays messages: startup/rotation/decision state and transcript writes must distinguish replay from new work. Production latest-only AD recovery, missing latest transcript with older history, replay deduplication, stale events and failed rotation remain planned acceptance work; they are not proved by successful load.
